chapter: Small band, Charlie Parker and the big band
title: Hearing Mary Lou Williams, Basie and other big bands
summary: He first heard Mary Lou Williams with Andy Kirk at Fairyland Park and caught Basie's group when they returned; Ben Webster and Lester were gone.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well, and also, you had quite a lot of big bands in Kansas City. I mean, you --
Right, never got a chance to hear big bands.
When did you first hear Mary?
Mary Lou? First time I heard Mary Lou, Andy Kirk played two nights, I think, a Friday and Saturday night out at the Fairyland Park (PHONETIC.)
And so when I heard they was going to be in town, I went out there that night.
You'd heard about Mary, had you?
You had heard about Mary, had you?
Oh yes, I knew about here, reading about her in DownBeat and everything, you know.
And her records and so forth.

So I got a chance to go down here and hear her and when Basie came in town, I got a chance to catch Basie's group, you know, and when come in, I got a chance to hear their group. You know, big bands that came in, you know. And --
And what all guys were you listening to in Kansas City? Was Ben there then?
Yes. During these times, I think Ben must have been playing with Ellington.
And Lester, of course, was with Basie.
And Lester was gone, you know. I never heard Lester, only when I heard him with Basie.
